posts.title: Planning study on a single course, a bundle, or all-access
posts.excerpt: The three plans differ by courses, access, mock exams, live Q&A, and feedback, and the certificate at the end is a certificate of completion from Shikaku Academy.
posts.content:
Shikaku Academy was founded in 2017 for people who want to prepare for a widely recognised project-management or IT credential while they keep a job. The school is fully online. Lessons are recorded at the studio and support office at Kade 14, 3072 Rotterdam, Netherlands, then played in the lesson player. You do not travel to a classroom, and you do not wait for a group to gather. You choose a course or a plan, pay by card, and begin.

The catalogue has six courses and two pathways. On project management: Project Delivery Foundations, 24 lessons, 18 hours, $149; Agile Practitioner Track, 20 lessons, 15 hours, $169; and Advanced Project Leadership, 32 lessons, 26 hours, $229. On IT: Cloud Fundamentals, 22 lessons, 16 hours, $159; IT Service Management Essentials, 26 lessons, 20 hours, $179; and Network & Security Basics, 28 lessons, 22 hours, $189. The shortest recording is 15 hours and the longest is 26 hours. Those figures are lesson time, not a timetable the academy sets. A working week can hold one lesson or several. A progress marker shows how far through the list you have come.

There are three ways to buy, and the differences are concrete. A single course starts at $149, includes that one course, and lasts 12 months. You get one mock exam, live Q&A monthly, a study planner, and a certificate of completion. You do not get instructor feedback on two assignments. A pathway bundle is $429 for the three courses of one track, either project management or IT, and lasts 18 months. Mock exams cover the track, live Q&A is weekly, and feedback on two assignments is included. All-access is $690 for all six courses and lasts 24 months, with mock exams for every course, weekly live Q&A, and the same feedback. Live Q&A, whichever plan you hold, is on Wednesdays at 19:00 CET.

The path through the school is four steps. First, choose the course or the plan, using the lesson counts and hours rather than a slogan. Second, pay at checkout by card. Prices are in USD, and VAT is shown at checkout. Third, learn in the lesson player at your pace, inside the access period. Fourth, take the mock exam and download your certificate of completion. If you have chosen badly, you can ask for a refund within 14 days, provided you have watched less than 20 percent. That rule is the same on every plan. It is a way out of a mistaken purchase. It is not a promise about what the course will do for your work.

Learner support is led by Priya Raman and is open Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 18:00 CET, and Saturday from 09:00 to 13:00 CET. The address is support@shikaku-academy.example. A question about a lesson can wait for Wednesday, or it can go to the desk sooner if you are blocked. The people behind the courses are a team of seven. Helena Marsh is founder and director of studies. Tomasz Wierzbicki teaches courses 01 and 03. Amara Osei teaches Agile Practitioner Track. Rafael Quintero teaches Cloud Fundamentals. Ingrid Solberg teaches IT Service Management Essentials. Daniel Mwangi teaches Network & Security Basics.

It is worth being exact about the certificate. Shikaku Academy issues a certificate of completion for the course you finished. That is the academy's own document. It is not a credential awarded by an outside body, and the site does not name those bodies or claim their marks. The courses are written to prepare you for widely recognised project-management and IT credentials. Preparation is not the same thing as sitting someone else's exam. The academy does not publish a pass rate, and it does not publish a salary. A longer plan buys more courses and more months. It does not buy a different kind of certificate.

The three stories on the site are specific for the same reason. Lucía Ferrer moved from operations coordinator to project coordinator and took the project-management bundle. Jonas Becker moved from help-desk analyst to service desk lead and took IT Service Management Essentials. Noor Haddad was returning to work, is now a cloud support associate, and took Cloud Fundamentals. Each account names a person, two roles, and a course. None of them is a rate you can apply to yourself. Read them as three finished accounts, then go back to the price list if you are still deciding.

A calm week of study is ordinary. Open My courses, play the next lesson, and stop when your time is gone. Note one question for Wednesday if your plan includes that session. Use the study planner to see the lessons that remain. When the list is finished, take the mock exam included with the course and download the certificate of completion if you are done. Then decide whether the next course, if your plan has one, should start now or later. Access is long enough to allow that decision: 12 months, 18 months, or 24 months, according to the plan you paid for.

The office in Rotterdam is a studio and a support desk, not a campus. You can finish an entire pathway without seeing it. If you want a person before you pay, write to the support address during the hours above and name the course you are considering. The answer you should expect is factual: lessons, hours, price, access, and what the certificate is. That is the whole offer, and it is the same offer in every corner of the site.
